_comment: Local executor baked parameters (P0 price-type signals). This file is the SINGLE source of truth for the thresholds: scripts/build_local_executor.py bakes it into qmt_gateway/local_executor.py (PARAMS block) and the builder refuses to build when the baked copy has drifted. Every threshold here must appear in the baked PARAMS table; the rule layer of local_executor.py may not contain a bare numeric literal at all.
_comment_windows: Time windows are 'HH:MM' strings in Beijing time. no_cancel_windows = windows where cancelling is forbidden (e.g. right before the close, where a cancel that does not settle can leave a live order behind). no_new_order_windows = windows where placing a new order is forbidden (e.g. the call auction, where a limit order can be matched at a price nobody intended).
_comment_broker: This executor is the LOCAL process: it runs outside QMT on the physical Windows box, so it may read local files and use the network. It never touches the QMT built-in strategy sandbox.
_comment_ids: The signal short code is <signal_codes[kind]><symbol head> and travels in every order remark as <version>-<short code>; it is the idempotency key rebuilt from the broker's own same-day order table.
_comment_nontrading: non_trading_weekdays uses Python weekday numbering (0=Monday .. 6=Sunday). closed_days is the fallback when no Go-produced trading_calendar.json is reachable; a real calendar file adds to it at runtime.

LnMktCap.missing_input: total share count series (share capital panel)

lu_early_seal.missing_input: first seal minute + break count (THS pool)

_comment_arm: rule_arm maps a ported rule kind to 'shadow' | 'live' | 'off'. Default for anything not listed is 'off' (it computes nothing, spends nothing), and the four builtin_rules above are always 'live' because that is today's behaviour. Why a knob at all instead of 'port it and it trades': the migration plan requires each re-calibrated rule to run in shadow against the Go engine for >=5 trading days first -- a threshold re-calibrated wrong changes the strategy's MEANING without changing any number a human would notice.
_comment_ported_modules: Names of the ported rule modules the builder must inline (rules_form/rules_ladder/rules_factor/rules_t/rules_sizing). Empty list = only the builtin four, i.e. today's behaviour. A name listed here whose file is missing, or whose registered kind has no short code in signal_codes, fails the build rather than publishing a smaller rule set.
_comment_signal_codes_added: 由 tools 一次性按模块 RULES 表生成（短码唯一性当场判），rule_arm 对新移植规则缺省 shadow：P1 阈值必须先与引擎对照 >=5 交易日。
_comment_derived: Written by scripts/derive_carrier_params.py --write. Three sources, in priority order: (1) the Go factory defaults, printed by cmd/derive_carrier_params and listed by --emit-derived-keys -- never hand-edit those, change the Go default and re-run; (2) aliases (t_direction_mode, the T-side window copies, breadth_missing_default) which rename an existing key and must never carry their own number; (3) qmt_gateway/rules_sizing.py SIZING_DEFAULTS rows for knobs the Go side has not exported a readout for yet -- each is registered with a reason in the script, and --check compares every overlapping row against Go. A key in none of the three is reported as DERIVE_UNHOUSED rather than quietly defaulted.
_comment_universe: params.symbols is the carrier's observation universe. Landed by scripts/derive_carrier_params.py --universe-from --write from the operator's watchlist/signal files; the repo default is two placeholder codes. The downlink package channel that would refresh this daily is not built, so re-run this command after any watchlist change you want the box to see.
